title: Live repro: parallel agents contend on the shared checkout — isolation is not airtight
summary: During the first parallel dispatch (6 agents, hold-merge), the onboard-dropin agent reported its live checkout HEAD moved under it because a concurrent agent (auto-extract-decisions) was operating on a shared branch / the live checkout rather than a fully isolated worktree. hold-merge still protected main (no agent merged), but agents were NOT isolated from each other — exactly the failure mode task #4 (harden git-worktree isolation) targets. Evidence: this is the live reproduction motivating #4's lease/lock-per-worktree + branch-per-task work. Integrator takeaway: until #4 lands, treat concurrent attempts on overlapping files as un-isolated and serialize file-coupled dispatch. Also note a merge STACK formed: onboard-dropin is stacked on orch/attempt/onboarding-kb (deps 7&8 not in main) — merge onboarding-kb first.
